# Judith Chapter 7 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Judith 7 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/JDT_007_page_001.jpg

---

**7:1** The following day Holofernes ordered his entire army and all his allied forces to march against Bethulia, seize the passes into the hill country, and make war on the Israelites.

**7:2** Every able-bodied man broke camp that day. Their combined forces numbered one hundred and seventy thousand infantry and twelve thousand cavalry, not counting the supply train and the men serving on foot — an exceedingly great multitude.

**7:3** They encamped in the valley near Bethulia, beside the spring, spreading out as far as Dothaim in breadth and from Bethulia to Cyamon in length — from Cyamon, which faces Esdraelon.

**7:4** When the Israelites saw their vast numbers, they were deeply dismayed and said to one another, "These men will devour the whole face of the land; neither the high mountains nor the valleys nor the hills can sustain the weight of their forces."

**7:5** Each man took up his weapons of war, they lit signal fires on their towers, and they remained on watch throughout that night.

**7:6** On the second day Holofernes led out all his cavalry before the Israelites in Bethulia,

**7:7** reconnoitered the approaches to their city, located the water sources, seized them, and posted armed detachments over them, then returned to his troops.

**7:8** Then all the chieftains of the Edomites and all the leaders of the Moabites and the commanders of the coastal peoples came to him and said:

**7:9** "Let our lord hear a word, so that his army does not suffer a defeat.

**7:10** For these Israelites do not rely on their spears but on the height of the mountains where they live; it is no easy matter to scale the peaks of their mountains.

**7:11** Therefore, lord, do not engage them in open battle, and not a single man of your force will fall.

**7:12** Stay in your camp, keeping every man of your army safe, and have your servants hold the spring that flows from the foot of the mountain —

**7:13** for that is where all the inhabitants of Bethulia get their water. Thirst will destroy them and they will surrender the city. Meanwhile, we and our troops will ascend the summits of the nearby mountains and camp there to make sure not one man leaves the city.

**7:14** They will waste away — they and their wives and their children — and before the sword ever strikes them they will be laid out in the streets where they live.

**7:15** And you will exact bitter payment from them for their rebellion, for not receiving you in peace."

**7:16** These words pleased Holofernes and all his attendants, and he ordered that it be done as they had proposed.

**7:17** The Ammonite contingent moved out, along with five thousand Assyrians; they encamped in the valley and seized the water sources and springs of the Israelites.

**7:18** The Edomites and Ammonites went up and encamped in the hill country opposite Dothan; some were sent southward and eastward, toward Egrebel near Chous, which lies by the stream of Mochmur. The rest of the Assyrian army encamped in the plain, covering the entire face of the land. Their tents and equipment formed an enormous encampment — a very great multitude.

**7:19** The Israelites cried out to the Lord their God, for their spirits sank; every one of their enemies had surrounded them and there was no way of escape from their midst.

**7:20** The whole Assyrian army remained encamped around them — infantry, chariots, and cavalry — for thirty-four days, until every water jar belonging to the inhabitants of Bethulia was empty,

**7:21** the cisterns were running dry, and they did not have enough water to drink even for a single day; it was being rationed out by measure.

**7:22** The children were dispirited, and the women and young men were collapsing from thirst, falling in the streets of the city and in the gateways. There was no strength left in them at all.

**7:23** Then all the people gathered against Uzziah and the city rulers — the young men, the women, and the children — and they cried out in a loud voice before all the elders:

**7:24** "May God judge between us and you! For you have done us great wrong in refusing to make peace with the Assyrians.

**7:25** And now there is no one to help us. God has sold us into their hands, to be laid prostrate before them in thirst and utter ruin.

**7:26** So now summon them and surrender the whole city as plunder to the forces of Holofernes and his entire army.

**7:27** It is better for us to be their plunder. Yes, we will be enslaved — but our lives will be spared, and we will not have to watch our infants die before our eyes or see our wives and children breathe their last.

**7:28** We call heaven and earth and our God, the Lord of our ancestors, to witness against you — he who punishes us for our sins and the sins of our ancestors — that he should not carry out such a thing this day."

**7:29** Then there was loud weeping from the whole assembly, and they cried out to the Lord God with a great voice.

**7:30** Uzziah said to them, "Take courage, brothers — hold out five more days, during which the Lord our God may yet turn his compassion toward us, for he will not abandon us completely.

**7:31** But if those days pass and no help comes, I will do as you have said."

**7:32** He dismissed the people, each man to his post, and they went back to the walls and towers of the city. The women and children he sent home. And they were in great distress throughout the city.
